$comment: workflow-enablement.json -- every workflow whose forge state is NOT active.
Enforcer: src/Core.TypeScript/ci/workflow-enablement.ts, run in the drift (loud) job.
A disabled workflow sits at its correct path, is valid YAML, is named by prose and by
rosters, and produces ZERO runs. No run means no red X, so it is the vacuity class in its
purest administrative form -- and every workflow guard in this repo reads TEXT, so none of
them can see it. The state lives only in the forge.

THIS FILE IS A RECORD, NOT A DEFECT LIST. An entry does not demand that the lane be switched back on; several of these were stopped deliberately because they committed to the repo on every run and were growing it. The point of the row is that the silence is legible.
The audit goes RED when: a non-active workflow is missing here (the next silent
disablement); an entry here is active again (a stale row hides the next real one); an entry
names a path the forge does not list; an entry has no reason or a bad classification.

classifications.intentional: A maintainer decided this lane should not run, and the reason says why. Recorded for visibility, never as a defect list.
classifications.unreviewed: Measured non-active with no recorded decision. Reported as a warning on every run until someone classifies it. NOT a backlog: the remedy may well be `intentional`.

entries.reason: INTENTIONAL, maintainer decision (Aaron, 2026-09-09): these cadence/heartbeat lanes were stopped because they were growing the Zeta repository uncontrollably. Several hold contents:write and COMMIT on every scheduled run -- drift-sweep.yml writes a tick event to docs/drift-events/ per cadence, which is exactly the growth this decision removed. Re-enabling any of them resumes that growth, so re-enablement is NOT the remedy and is not proposed here. This row exists so the lane's silence is VISIBLE rather than invisible: a workflow that produces no runs can produce no red X, and nothing else in this repository can see that. If a lane's function is ever wanted back, it needs a NON-COMMITTING host -- a design note for later, not a defect now.
